subject: Service incident: transient model routing failures — customer update
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 01:12:00 -0700
Subject: ALERT: SEV-2 detected — model routing errors increasing

Team,

We are seeing a spike in model routing failures across the us-east serving pool starting ~00:58 PDT. Error rate for generation requests to the primary routing tier has climbed to ~6% (baseline ~0.1%) and a subset of customers are seeing request timeouts. Latency is elevated but not wholesale failure yet.

What we know:
- Affected surface: text-generation routes for the gpt-cci family using the routing layer.
- On-call SRE (Arnold) has applied a temporary rule to bypass a degraded routing node; partial mitigation observed.
- PagerDuty: PD-8762 (acknowledged).

Immediate asks:
1) Start a command-post (phone + Slack channel) for coordination — David, can you host?
2) Draft a short customer-facing note (one-paragraph impact, what we are doing, ETA).
3) Prepare logs snapshot and a short mitigation checklist we can attach.

Attachments: logs_snapshot_20270519.txt (key traces)

Ben
Senior SRE
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 01:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ALERT: SEV-2 detected — model routing errors increasing

Thanks — we're on it. David, I can pull together a one-paragraph executive note and get it reviewed by Product. Suggested copy below — feel free to paste to NimbusPay with any edits.

Suggested customer note (draft):
Hi Samantha — we detected elevated request errors impacting a subset of text-generation traffic in the US region. Our engineers have identified a routing-tier degradation and applied a temporary bypass; this reduced errors but not fully resolved. We're working on a permanent fix now and will share an ETA in the next 30–45 minutes. Full postmortem and next steps will be provided within 72 hours.

Also: CT0 (cto@nimbuspay.com) is on the escalation path; recommend cc'ing them.

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@ops.nimbuspay.com>
Cc: NimbusPay CTO <cto@nimbuspay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 01:40:00 -0700
Subject: Service incident: transient model routing failures — customer update

Samantha —

I’m writing to confirm we have detected elevated error rates impacting a subset of generation requests in the US region that may be affecting some of your calls. Our engineers have identified the root cause as a routing-tier degradation that intermittently misroutes requests to a degraded node.

What we have done so far:
- Applied an emergency bypass to the affected routing node (partial mitigation; error rate reduced from ~6% to ~1.5%).
- Scoped impacted customers and verified that the majority of traffic is now routing correctly.
- Raised the incident to SEV-1 for full remediation priority and staffed a command-post.

What we are doing next (ETA):
- Deploying a configuration and routing policy change to prevent the flawed route selection (ETA 45 minutes).
- Running additional automated validation against NimbusPay traffic patterns to confirm stability (ETA immediately after deploy).
- Collecting full logs and preparing a postmortem (deliverable within 72 hours).

Impact summary for you:
- Possible transient 5–10% increase in request errors for generation routes between 00:58–01:40 PDT, with partial mitigation in place. Most requests are passing after the bypass; we will confirm when rates return to baseline.

Attachments: incident_summary_v1.pdf (one-page impact/mitigation), mitigation_playbook.md

We will provide a brief follow-up within 30–45 minutes with an updated ETA. Please reply if you have any immediate concerns or if you prefer a dedicated call — we can stand one up now.

Regards,
David Kim
Head of Technical Account Management
Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: NimbusPay incident — postmortem timeline and owners

Team —

Quick follow-up after yesterday’s command-post and the customer-facing update. Summary and next steps for the postmortem:

Summary:
- Incident escalated to SEV-1 at 01:22 PDT when we saw sustained elevated error rates after initial bypass.
- Root cause (preliminary): routing selection algorithm regression under specific sequence-length distribution when combined with a stale kernel on node pool A.
- Customer impact window: 00:58–02:05 PDT; observed error spike peaked ~01:10–01:30 PDT.

Owners and deliverables:
- Postmortem lead: Stephanie Nguyen — write-up due EOD Friday (2027-05-21).
- SRE remediation: Ben Carter — permanent routing policy patch and kernel upgrade scheduled for Thu 11:00 PDT.
- Customer comms: Marissa Cole — send postmortem summary to NimbusPay and confirm any compensatory credits (if required).

Action items (short):
1) Stephanie: collect timeline + RCA + evidence links (Drive link in related_links).
2) Ben: confirm scheduled kernel roll and provide rollback plan.
3) Marissa: coordinate postmortem delivery and cc legal if customer requests credits.

I’ll be available for any escalations and will loop-in Product if scope of regression suggests a broader model family risk.

-David
Head of Technical Account Management
Redwood Inference
